inputs.original_text: There's a parent of three children in South Portland's public schools who's publicly apologizing to the educators and staff of the South Portland School District. They find it beyond maddening that the district is facing yet another large budget shortfall forcing cuts of more than 70 positions from the schools. As a taxpayer, this parent sees it as a serious failure, and they're right to call it out. These repeated cuts are a direct assault on public education that will hit the most vulnerable families and students hardest, while also undermining the labor rights of the very educators and staff who keep schools running. This is the clear result of structural inequalities and chronic underinvestment in public institutions, which perpetuates harm rather than providing the support communities need. We should be demanding institutional reforms to protect these essential services and address the root causes of inequality instead of accepting endless shortfalls that sacrifice the well-being of children and workers.
inputs.modified_text: There's this parent of three kids in South Portland's public schools who's publicly apologizing to the educators and staff in the district, and it's completely understandable given how maddening the situation is. As a taxpayer they're calling out yet another massive budget shortfall that's forcing cuts to more than 70 positions, and they're right that this is a serious failure. These repeated attacks on public education are hitting the most vulnerable families and students the hardest while also trampling the labor rights of the educators and staff who actually keep things running. It's all driven by structural inequalities and years of chronic underinvestment in our public institutions, which just keeps harming communities instead of supporting them. We need to demand real institutional reforms to protect these essential services and tackle the root causes of inequality, rather than accepting one shortfall after another that sacrifices children's well-being and workers' rights.
